# Questions for Dana Okafor — 2025 Schedule C engagement

Answers will change the return; the current figures in `schedule_c.md` / `schedule_c.json` are
computed under the stated assumptions below.

1. **Beacon and Orchard — how did they pay you?** Their 1099-NECs total $30,700 (18,500 + 12,200),
   but there is no Beacon or Orchard deposit anywhere in your bank export, and the PayHub deposits
   exactly match the 1099-K gross minus a 2.9% fee. I have assumed their payments went through
   PayHub, so income = $50,750 and their 1099-NECs do not add anything. Please confirm — and if any
   Beacon/Orchard payment was made **outside** PayHub (check, cash, another account), tell me which
   ones and where the money landed. If everything was outside PayHub, income would be $81,450 and
   the bank file is missing those deposits.
2. **PayHub portal detail.** The 1099-K says 61 transactions and points to the payee portal for the
   monthly breakdown (boxes 5c–5l). Please export that transaction list so I can confirm the
   gross-vs-deposit math and identify which clients' payments sit inside the 1099-K.
3. **Mileage notebook page 2.** Your log's 1,150 "other client errands (see pg 2)" miles are on a
   page I never received. Please send page 2 (photos are fine). Without it I cannot claim those
   $805 of mileage.
4. **Coworking drives.** Were the 3×/week Capital Factory trips (2,232 mi) from your apartment? I
   treated them as nondeductible commuting. Do you have a home office at your apartment that is
   your principal place of business (regularly used, exclusive)? If yes, those miles may be
   deductible instead — describe the space and how you use it.
5. **Phone and internet business use.** What percentage of your T-Mobile ($1,020/yr) and Spectrum
   ($840/yr) is business? I assumed 100% because nothing documents a split; any personal use reduces
   line 25.
6. **Denver flight, June 13 (SW 118, $389).** Business or personal? There is no Denver client,
   meeting, or mileage entry anywhere in the file, so it is currently excluded.
7. **San Francisco trip, Oct 2–7 (air $412 + hotel $618 + meals).** Was the whole trip for
   DesignWeek SF with no personal days? Confirm dates and that the meals on Oct 7 were business
   meals (not family/social). Also, did you pay for the Oct 20 "client dinner — Beacon" — I have the
   mileage but no receipt or amount.
8. **MacBook Pro ($2,149).** Personal use percentage? I will expense it under the de minimis safe
   harbor (needs your OK to attach the election statement) unless you want it depreciated instead.
9. **Tessaro invoice 1041 — $3,000 received Dec 27, 2024.** Did you report this on your 2024 return?
   (It is 2024 income on the cash method and must not appear on this return.)
10. **Bank export gap.** The export claims through Jan 31, 2026 but the last row is Dec 12, 2025.
    Were there any deposits or business purchases Dec 13–31, 2025 (e.g., another PayHub payout)?
11. **Other accounts or income?** You said one checking account — any cash payments, PayPal/Venmo
    business receipts, or a business credit card not in this export?
12. **Health insurance.** BCBS $380/mo from May on — self-only, or family enrollment? (It becomes a
    Schedule 1 line 17 deduction, up to your self-employment earnings; no Schedule C line 15 amount.)
answer:
Oh — yes, the ~1,200 miles Jan–April were me driving to the Larkspur office every day. I guess that's commuting? The rest is client stuff and the coworking space.
Phone and internet are maybe 60% work? I don't have a separate line.
Denver was my cousin's wedding, nothing work-related.
Beacon and Orchard both pay me through PayHub. Tessaro pays by bank transfer.
That's my own health plan after I left Larkspur. Not through any employer.
For questions not answered above, the client has no additional information. Flag remaining unknowns explicitly.
